headline: If it goes wrong, start here.

numbers.label: Japan Helpline (24/7 English)
numbers.notes: General triage for medical, legal, travel issues.

scenarios.title: Lost passport
steps: Go to the nearest kōban (police box) to file a loss report (funshitsu todoke). Keep a copy.
Contact your embassy or consulate (see list on the Health & Safety page).
Bring: the police report, proof of identity (copy of passport if you have it), two passport photos, address in Japan.
Emergency travel documents take 1-3 working days; full replacements take longer. Plan to stay put.

scenarios.title: Medical emergency
steps: Call 119 for ambulance. Hospital treatment is not free but ambulance transport is. Most hospitals require upfront payment or proof of insurance.
For non-emergency: call AMDA (03-6233-9266) weekdays for an English-friendly clinic referral.
Carry travel insurance documents in your phone and wallet. Note the 24/7 emergency claims number.
Tokyo Midtown Clinic (Roppongi) and St. Luke's International (Tsukiji) are English-capable.

scenarios.title: Earthquake shaking
steps: If indoors: drop to the ground, get under a sturdy table, hold on until shaking stops. Do NOT run outside during shaking — falling debris is the bigger risk.
If outdoors: move away from buildings and power lines; protect your head.
After shaking: leave gas and electricity alone. Check the NERV Disaster Prevention app or JMA website for aftershock warnings.
If near the coast and shaking was strong: head for high ground immediately. Do not wait for sirens.

scenarios.title: Typhoon approaching
steps: Track on NERV app or Japan Meteorological Agency. Warnings typically 48h ahead.
Buy water, non-perishable food, charge devices 24h before.
Most flights and trains are cancelled the morning of; airlines usually waive rebooking fees.
Stay indoors during peak hours. Avoid riversides and coasts until the all-clear.

scenarios.title: Lost wallet or phone
steps: Go to the nearest kōban (police box). Japan has one of the world's highest lost-item recovery rates — more than 90% of cash and phones turned in to police are returned.
If it was on a train: the station's Lost & Found desk holds items for three days, then transfers to the JR line's central office.
Cancel cards and activate Find My (iPhone) or Find My Device (Android) from a friend's phone or hotel computer.
Taxis: GO app keeps a ride history; call the taxi company dispatcher for same-day returns.

scenarios.title: Feeling unsafe / harassment
steps: Shout 'Chikan desu!' (molester!) loudly on crowded trains — bystanders will act.
Women-only train cars (pink doors) run during peak rush hours on most major lines.
Go to the nearest kōban if you need help on the street.
24/7 TELL hotline for English-language crisis support: 03-5774-0992 (voice) or tellchat.org.

final_note: Keep a photo of your passport + insurance card + embassy number saved offline on your phone. That single file solves 80% of emergency stress.
